checks.result: 8 browser tests before the final backend-only queued-recovery change

proof: One main slot is reserved alongside two background slots; evaluation has a separate admission class.
The third background Work remains durably queued with no worker job or model call until a background slot releases.
Four Works have distinct execution sessions; stopping one background Work leaves main and another background approval unchanged.
Main/background kind is pinned by the Store CAS, and request receipts still return the original Work.
Restart re-admits a queued command without replaying previously running sessions.
limitations: Workspace reservation and global model-call semaphore are not yet implemented; the test only proves a queued Work does not start a worker/model call.
Learning priority, configurable slot bounds, wall time budgets, durable inbox and full setting/workspace snapshots remain pending.
Recovery test seeds a queued crash boundary in an isolated fixture after graceful shutdown; actual power-loss behavior is not asserted.
Ubuntu and strict browser egress remain unverified; global acceptance statuses remain not_run.
No live paid model or remote repository action was performed.
